### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. spondyloperipheral dysplasia  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.791)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-186797, Reactome:R-HSA-198933, Reactome:R-HSA-2022090, Reactome:R-HSA-216083, Reactome:R-HSA-3000171)

**Proposed mechanism:** COL2A1 (HGNC:2200) —DISRUPTS→ Type II collagen synthesis and extracellular matrix formation (GO:0005576); Type II collagen synthesis and extracellular matrix formation (GO:0005576) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0004325); Type II collagen synthesis and extracellular matrix formation (GO:0005576) —LEADS_TO→ Short limb skeletal dysplasia (HP:0005744); Type II collagen synthesis and extracellular matrix formation (GO:0005576) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004322). Mutations in COL2A1 disrupt the normal synthesis and assembly of type II collagen, a critical component of the extracellular matrix in cartilage and bone. This disruption leads to a spectrum of skeletal dysplasias, including short limb and short stature phenotypes, common to both spondylometaphyseal dysplasia, Schmidt type and spondyloperipheral dysplasia.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in COL2A1 that are specific to one disease but not the other, or identification of distinct molecular pathways or genes driving the phenotypes independently, would falsify this shared mechanism hypothesis. _(variant: The presence of common benign variants in COL2A1 in the general population (gnomAD > 1%) that overlap with reported disease-causing variants would call into question the pathogenicity of those specific variants.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in COL2A1 for these skeletal dysplasias could facilitate the development of targeted therapies aimed at improving collagen synthesis or function, potentially benefiting patients with either condition. Furthermore, it aids in differential diagnosis and genetic counseling.
